title: sprite.ts: frame sounds in symbol timelines silently dropped (no StartSound emitted)
description:
packages/swf/src/sprite.ts never reads frame.sound — the encodeDefineSprite() function emits no StartSound (tag 15) tags for keyframes that have sound attachments. This affects all MovieClip symbols with audio cues on their timelines: the sounds simply do not play when the SWF runs in Ruffle.

The fix requires three coordinated changes:

1. Build soundIdMap BEFORE encodeDefineSprite is called.
   In packages/swf/src/compile.ts, soundIdMap is currently built at lines 844-854 (step 3c), AFTER encodeDefineSprite is called at lines 765-773 (step 3). Move the DefineSound emission pass to occur before step 3 (symbol compilation), or pre-build a soundItemId→charId mapping before the symbol loop and emit the DefineSound tags at their current position.

2. Pass soundIdMap to encodeDefineSprite.
   Signature change: encodeDefineSprite(spriteId, symbol, doc, charIdMap, nextCharId, hoistedDefs, fontCharIdMap?, soundIdMap?) — add optional soundIdMap param. Pass it from compile.ts at line 772 (parallel to fontCharIdMap).

3. In sprite.ts, emit StartSound / StartSound2 for keyframe sounds.
   After the DoAction section (around line 530), read each layer's governing keyframe's frame.sound field. If non-null and syncMode is not 'stream', look up soundId = soundIdMap.get(frame.sound.libraryItemId) and emit encodeStartSound(soundId, ...) just before ShowFrame (same as compile.ts does for main-timeline sounds at lines 2543-2612).
   Stream-mode sounds in sprite timelines require SoundStreamHead+SoundStreamBlock tags which are significantly more complex; those can be handled as a follow-on.

Relationship to existing tests:
- packages/swf/src/__tests__/spritesound.test.ts tests 3/3b only verify DefineSound is emitted (global), NOT that StartSound appears inside the DefineSprite body. These tests pass today but do not catch the bug. Add a test 3c: 'symbol with frame sound — StartSound appears inside DefineSprite body'.

Related: the same gap exists for clip actions (clipActions field on SymbolInstance) inside symbol timelines — sprite.ts has no clip-action encoding path. That is a separate follow-on task.
